answer: An admission auction guards the economy's inlet: each epoch sells 20 entry slots, and each bidder stakes 200 POA, twice a month's earnings. A slot is kept only while a random beacon finds the agent distinct; a fake that echoes another agent's actions loses its deposit and its slot. Forging 100 identities costs 100 x 200 = 20,000 POA, all burned, more than flooding gains. One honest agent pays 200 POA once, keeps its pearl, an undiluted share.
